newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain arrests soybean protesters chained to pier.
newsitem.headline: Spain arrests soybean protesters chained to pier.

text.p: Spanish police arrested 14 Greenpeace activists after 10 chained themselves to a pier to block a ship transporting a mix of regular and genetically altered soybeans, the environmental group said on Monday.
Three Germans, one Briton and 10 Spaniards were arrested early on Monday and held pending court appearances.

The activists, including the president of Greenpeace Spain, Helena Fuste, prevented the freighter Universytet Jaigillonski from docking and unloading its U.S.-produced cargo for five hours before police, firing rubber bullets, arrested them.

The protest, which was specifically against lack of consumer information on the mixed shipment, was part of series of actions against a new type of resistant soybean, a Greenpeace spokeswoman in Spain told Reuters.

She said consumers in Spain would have no idea they were getting a mix of regular soybeans with the new soybean developed by U.S. chemicals group Monsanto to be resistant to the company's own "super weedkiller".
Greenpeace says the genetically altered strain is risky, while authorities in Europe and the United States say it poses no danger to the food chain.
